title: RowContrastDetection mode params
description: Per-row cross-sectional std/variance signal. Highlights rows with large pixel variation across the ROI width — characteristic of a liquid meniscus or tip-edge transition. Complementary to IntensityDetection (mean-based).

stat.description:
Which per-row statistic to compute.

'std' (default) — standard deviation of pixel values within each row (horizontal). High where a scanline contains many alternating bright/dark patches.

'variance' — squared std within each row (horizontal). Same as 'std' but amplifies large deviations more.

'std_v' — local sliding-window std of the per-row mean along the z-axis (vertical). High where mean intensity changes rapidly between adjacent rows — a vertical edge detector.

'variance_v' — squared version of std_v (vertical).

'peak_count_h' — number of significant peaks in each row's intensity profile, normalised by row width^exponent. Counts only peaks meeting the minimum distance and prominence thresholds. Distinguishes rows with many distinct features from flat rows.

'peak_prominence_sum_h' — sum of peak prominences in each row, normalised by row width^exponent. Rewards rows with large-amplitude oscillations (tall peaks) over rows that are merely noisy (many tiny bumps).

vertical_window_px.description: Window size (in rows) for the vertical sliding-window std computation. Only used when stat = 'std_v' or 'variance_v'. Larger values smooth out single-row noise at the cost of vertical resolution.

variance_cap.description: Maximum value to clamp the output signal when stat = 'variance' or 'variance_v'. 0 = disabled. Setting a cap prevents a single bright or edge artefact from dominating the signal scale and compressing all other features toward zero. Useful when the region of interest has an unavoidable high-variance spot (e.g. a reflection at one end of the ROI).

peak_min_distance.description: Minimum horizontal separation in pixels between two counted peaks in the same row. Prevents a broad peak from being counted multiple times. Only used when stat = 'peak_count_h' or 'peak_prominence_sum_h'.

peak_min_prominence.description: Minimum prominence (0–255 raw intensity units) for a local maximum to count as a peak. Prominence = how much you must descend from the peak before reaching a taller neighbour. Setting this above the noise floor filters out "rocky but flat" rows while keeping rows with genuine large swings. Only used when stat = 'peak_count_h' or 'peak_prominence_sum_h'.

peak_width_exponent.description: Width-normalisation exponent. The raw count (or prominence sum) is divided by row_width^exponent to correct for wider rows having more opportunity for more peaks. 0 = no normalisation, 0.5 = square-root dampening (recommended), 1.0 = fully per-pixel. Only used when stat = 'peak_count_h' or 'peak_prominence_sum_h'.

blur_method.description: Blur applied before computing per-row std. Smoothing reduces sensitivity to single-pixel noise spikes.

blur_kernel.description: Kernel size for Gaussian blur (must be odd). Only used when blur_method = 'gaussian'.

bilateral_d.description: Bilateral filter diameter. Only used when blur_method = 'bilateral'.

bilateral_sigma_color.description: Bilateral filter sigma in color space. Only used when blur_method = 'bilateral'.

bilateral_sigma_space.description: Bilateral filter sigma in coordinate space. Only used when blur_method = 'bilateral'.

use_ab.description: True = compute std of the accumulated A:B frame difference; False = single frame. A:B mode highlights rows that change between frames rather than rows that are always bright.

gradient_method.description: Optional Sobel gradient applied after blur before computing std. 'none' = disabled. 'y' (vertical gradient) is usually most useful for detecting horizontal transitions.

gradient_ksize.description: Sobel kernel size. Use 3, 5, or 7 (odd values only).

intensity_threshold.description: Normalised contrast minimum to count a row as a candidate (0–1). Applied after the signal is normalised to [0, 1].

min_distance.description: Minimum pixel distance between adjacent candidates.

roi_expansion_px.description: Expand (positive) or contract (negative) the calibrated ROI polygon outward by this many pixels before computing the signal. Negative values shave off the outer edges — useful for excluding tip-wall artefacts. 0 = use calibrated ROI exactly.

use_contrast.description: When true, subtract a blurred reference frame from the sample before all other processing. Useful for isolating changes due to liquid presence.

contrast_mode.description:
'absolute' — output = |sample − reference|.
'relative' — signed difference centred at grey (127).

contrast_blur_method.description: Blur applied independently to sample and reference before differencing.

contrast_blur_kernel.description: Gaussian kernel size for contrast pre-blur (must be odd). Only used when contrast_blur_method = 'gaussian'.

contrast_bilateral_d.description: Bilateral filter diameter for contrast pre-blur. Only used when contrast_blur_method = 'bilateral'.

contrast_bilateral_sigma_color.description: Bilateral sigma colour for contrast pre-blur.

contrast_bilateral_sigma_space.description: Bilateral sigma space for contrast pre-blur.

contrast_min.description: Minimum contrast threshold (0–255). Differences below this are suppressed.

contrast_max.description: Maximum contrast cap (0–255). Differences at or above this are saturated.
